discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, establishing moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional van der Waals and moiré materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would make the electronic bands nearly flat, so that interactions would dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group developed the tear-and-stack method needed to control twist angle precisely, confirmed the prediction, and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. Together these works showed that a new degree of freedom, the twist angle, lets physicists engineer quantum materials in which band structure, filling and interaction strength can all be tuned with a gate. This opened the field of moiré quantum matter. Hundreds of groups worldwide now use such systems to study Mott and Wigner crystal states, orbital ferromagnetism, and fractional quantum anomalous Hall effects without a magnetic field. Few recent discoveries have changed so deeply what we can create and measure in strongly correlated matter.
